title: Coronary CT angiography
also: CT scan of the heart arteries
what: Images of the heart's arteries on a CT scanner, with contrast dye into a vein. They show narrowing and plaques.
why: For chest pain, to check the heart arteries without a catheter, or when stress test results are unclear.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes in the room including prep; the scan itself takes a few seconds; the report in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: Allergy to iodine or contrast dye
Kidney disease, diabetes, and your diabetes medicines
The heart and blood pressure medicines you take
Asthma. It can affect the choice of medicine to slow your pulse
If you are or might be pregnant
If you have stents or had bypass surgery

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 3 to 4 hours. Water is fine. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Coffee
prepare.text: On the day of the scan, you are usually asked to skip coffee, strong tea, and energy drinks. They speed up your pulse.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your medicines on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide. Sometimes a pill is given before the scan to slow your pulse.

prepare.title: Blood test
prepare.text: A recent creatinine test is often needed.

steps: An IV line is put in a vein in your arm
Your pulse is checked. If it is fast, medicine is given to slow it
ECG stickers are put on your chest
Sometimes a pill or spray under the tongue is given to widen the arteries
You lie on the table and practice holding your breath on command
Contrast is given and images are taken. Hold your breath for a few seconds
After the scan, the IV line is removed
feel: It does not hurt, apart from the IV line
With contrast: a wave of warmth and a metallic taste
The spray under the tongue may cause a mild headache
after: Sit for 15 to 30 minutes under observation
Drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
The report usually comes in 1 to 2 days. Take it to a cardiologist
red_flags: Pressing chest pain for more than 15 minutes, shortness of breath, or cold sweat: call emergency services right away
After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services
The IV site becomes very swollen and painful

faq.q: Can CT replace a regular coronary angiogram?
faq.a: They are different methods. CT checks the arteries without a catheter. If a severe narrowing is found, a regular angiogram may be ordered.
The heart moves. With a slow pulse, the image is sharper.

faq.q: Can I have coffee in the morning?
faq.a: Usually not. It speeds up your pulse. Check with the clinic.

reminders.text: Coronary CT tomorrow. No coffee or strong tea in the morning. Bring your creatinine test and a list of your medicines.
